objective: Gate the open-water curve of the Potsdam Propeller Test Case VP1304 - thrust coefficient KT, torque coefficient KQ and open-water efficiency eta_O against advance ratio J - using simpleFoam with MRF against the SVA Potsdam Report 3752 tables, with the gate spec naming WHICH of that report's four differently-corrected tables is the reference
rationale: Two things make this the most tractable of the naval extensions, and one thing makes it riskier than the docket assumes. Tractable, first: the reference data is genuinely open. SVA Potsdam Report 3752 is free with attribution and carries full J, KT, 10KQ and eta tables plus polynomial fits, which is a stronger position than KP505, whose geometry is available but whose open-water data was searched for and not found openly, and far stronger than the Wageningen B-series, whose regression coefficients were searched for and are not openly obtainable. Tractable, second: the case is single-phase, submerged and steady, with no free surface, so it does not inherit the F7a ladder block at all and is the one naval item that can proceed today. Now the risk, and it corrects the docket. docs/DOCKET.md G4 says this reuses F8's MRF machinery. That claim was checked against F8's own dictionaries this session rather than repeated. What genuinely transfers: simpleFoam with an incompressible single-phase steady SIMPLE stack; constant/MRFProperties in exactly the cellZone, axis, origin, omega form F8 uses; snappyHexMesh from a triSurface STL; and the forces function object that already writes an integrated moment about a rotation axis, which is KT and KQ in all but name. What does NOT transfer, and the docket does not say: F8's fluid is air at nu 1.4805e-05 whereas a propeller runs in water near 1.0e-06, so the Reynolds number and hence the near-wall resolution requirement are different; F8's geometry is a UAE Phase VI wind-turbine blade STL and is not parametric, so a five-bladed high-skew propeller is entirely new geometry and is the dominant new work; F8 solved one operating point whereas an open-water curve is a sweep of six to eight advance ratios. Most importantly, F8's own gate returned NO VERDICT because the force history never settled - SIMPLE solution converged appears zero times in either of its logs. So what this case inherits from F8 is a solver stack with a known, unresolved settling problem, not a proven capability, and the pre-registration must treat settling as the primary risk rather than an afterthought
gate: Declared before any mesh exists. Reference, and this clause is the point: SVA Potsdam Report 3752 contains FOUR differently-corrected open-water tables which disagree materially, so the pre-registration must name WHICH table by its correction, with the page and the correction's own description quoted, and hash the source PDF. A gate citing SVA 3752 without that has named a document containing four answers, which is the same defect class F7a_REGATE_SPEC.md was written to retire. Stations: advance ratios frozen before the first solve, spanning the tabulated range and including the design point. Metric definition pinned in advance: the thrust and torque integration patches and whether hub and shaft are included, the rotation-axis and sign conventions, the reference diameter and revolution rate, and the non-dimensionalisation of KT, KQ and eta_O written as formulae not as names. Averaging window and transient-rejection rule declared in advance, with the settling test explicit. Three-valued verdict per docket B2: PASS if max deviation across the frozen advance ratios is inside the declared band for both KT and KQ on two mesh rungs, with the fine rung not worse; FAIL, reported as a result, if outside with settled histories; NO VERDICT if the settling test fails, which is what the nearest comparable case in this lab actually returned
cost_basis: estimate scaled from a measured sibling on the identical solver stack. F8_runs/phase6_mrf: 230,135 cells, 600 iterations, 4 ranks, 87 s wall = 5.8 core-min, read from F8_MRF_HAND2001_GATE.md and its logs. A propeller needs finer near-blade resolution than that rotor and needs more iterations because settling is the known risk, so the scaling is roughly 600,000 cells at 3,000 iterations, giving about 75 core-min per advance ratio. Priced as one feasibility point at 80, a seven-point coarse curve at about 530, and a two-point mesh-refinement check at about 300, totalling about 910 and rounded to 900. The dominant uncertainty is not the arithmetic but whether the forces settle at all; if they do not, the item stops early and spends far less. Graded against the measured cost afterwards per the charter's factor-three rule
expected_knowledge_gain: A propeller open-water curve is the single most recognisable marine validation artifact after hull resistance, and unlike every other item on this line it is not blocked by the F7a gate. Three outcomes, each changing a decision. A pass gives the marine line its first passing credential and simultaneously demonstrates that the MRF stack can settle, which retires the open question F8 left. A fail with settled forces bounds what the lab may claim for rotating machinery generally, not just for propellers. A no-verdict on settling would be the second independent case of the same failure on this stack and would convert an isolated F8 anomaly into a characterised instrument defect, which is worth more than the propeller curve itself and is why the settling test is written into the gate rather than left to judgement
hard_criterion_note: Extends the F8 MRF family - same solver, same MRF formulation, same force function object - but with new geometry, a different working fluid and a sweep rather than a single point. Filed as existing-family on the solver stack, with the geometry and the sweep declared as genuinely new work in the rationale rather than hidden inside the reuse claim
citations: SVA Potsdam Report 3752, Potsdam Propeller Test Case VP1304, open-water tables with J, KT, 10KQ and eta plus polynomial fits; free with attribution; verified accessible 2026-08-11. launch_prompt: Propeller open-water curve, PPTC VP1304, on simpleFoam plus MRF. NOT blocked by the F7a ladder - this is single-phase and submerged - so this is the naval item that can proceed first. Step 1, zero compute: read demo-output/website/campaign/F8_MRF_HAND2001_GATE.md in full, especially its settling failure and its pre-registered averaging window, then NAVAL_CAPABILITY_GAP_MAP.md and F7a_REGATE_SPEC.md. Step 2, zero compute: obtain SVA Report 3752, hash it, and identify all four corrected open-water tables; the pre-registration must name ONE by its correction, quoting the report's own description of it, and must state why that one. Do not proceed while the reference is a document rather than a table. Step 3: write the pre-registration - advance ratios, integration patches including whether hub and shaft count, sign conventions, KT/KQ/eta formulae written out, averaging window, transient-rejection rule, settling test, tolerance and its anchor. Step 4: geometry and mesh; the blade STL is new work, not an F8 edit. Step 5: one feasibility advance ratio, and STOP if the force history does not settle - report NO VERDICT and the instrument finding rather than sweeping. Step 6: the curve. Step 7: two-point mesh check. Budget 900 core-min with a hard stop at each stage boundary; setsid, launch_solve.sh registered, collector armed, nothing left running. Record: evidence file in demo-output/website/campaign/, birth certificate per docs/standards/MESH_STANDARD.md section 6, docket update, honest verdict.
